questions.prompt: What happens to files written to a container's writable layer when you run docker rm?

options.text: They are automatically moved to a volume
They are deleted along with the container
They are pushed to the registry
They stay on the host forever

questions.explanation: The writable layer is scratch space tied to the container. Removing the container deletes it, so durable data must live in a volume or bind mount.

questions.prompt: Which storage type is the recommended default for persisting a database's data?
questions.explanation: Named volumes are managed by Docker and persist independently of any container, making them the default choice for application and database data.

questions.prompt: When is a bind mount the best fit?

options.text: For portable data shared across many machines
For local development, so host edits appear instantly inside the container
For keeping secrets in memory only

questions.explanation: A bind mount maps a specific host folder into the container, so editing source on the host is instantly visible inside — ideal for local development. It is not portable across machines.

questions.prompt: A ______ mount stores data only in the host's memory and never writes it to disk. (one word)
questions.explanation: A tmpfs mount keeps data in memory only; it disappears when the container stops, which suits short-lived sensitive data.

questions.prompt: Which statements about volumes and bind mounts are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Named volumes are managed by Docker and are portable across machines
Bind mounts depend on exact host paths, so they are not portable
With -v, a missing bind-mount host path is silently created as an empty directory
Data in a named volume is deleted whenever its container is removed

questions.explanation: Volumes are Docker-managed and portable; bind mounts are host-path specific; -v silently creates a missing path. A volume persists after its container is removed (that is the point).

questions.prompt: Match each storage type to its best use.

pairs.right: In-memory scratch data never written to disk
Disposable scratch space for one container

questions.explanation: Volumes persist app data, bind mounts share host folders for dev, tmpfs keeps data in memory, and the writable layer is temporary per-container scratch space.
